---
title: "juphyter"
subtitle: "A Jupyter and Quarto kernel for PHP, built for statistical work with the phpstats packages"
jupyter: php
---

juphyter runs PHP in a notebook cell. It installs a Jupyter kernel, so
JupyterLab lists PHP in its launcher and Quarto executes `{php}` blocks in a
`.qmd`. The value a cell returns gets the richest representation the front end
can draw: a [phibble](https://github.com/phpstats/phibble) data frame becomes
an HTML table, a [phiz](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz) plot becomes a chart
or a static figure, and everything else gets a compact dump.

A notebook sees the project it sits in. The engine walks up from the notebook's
directory looking for `vendor/autoload.php`, so a notebook inside a Composer
project has that project's packages and its own classes in scope with no
configuration.

```{php}
#| echo: false
use Phibble\DataFrame;
use Phiz\Datasets;
use Phiz\Plot;
use function Phplyr\{group_by, summarise, arrange, desc, n, mean};
```

```{php}
$mpg = DataFrame::fromRows(Datasets::mpg());

$mpg
    |> group_by('class')
    |> summarise(models: n(), hwy: mean('hwy'))
    |> arrange(desc('hwy'));
```

```{php}
#| fig-cap: "Highway mileage falls as engine displacement rises."
Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())
    ->aes(x: 'displ', y: 'hwy', color: 'drv')
    ->point(opacity: 0.7)
    ->smooth(method: 'lm')
    ->labs(x: 'Displacement (L)', y: 'Highway mpg', color: 'Drive');
```

Both outputs above were produced by running the code above them in this page.
The site is rendered by `scripts/render-docs`, which executes every PHP cell
through the kernel.

## Install

```bash
composer require --dev phpstats/juphyter
vendor/bin/juphyter install
```

The install command writes one kernelspec where Jupyter looks for them and
prints where it went. It needs a Python installation that has `ipykernel`,
because the kernel is a Python transport in front of a PHP engine, and it
reports the exact `pip` command when that is missing. Several PHP versions can
be installed side by side, each under its own `--name`.

Static images from phiz plots need the
[vl-convert](https://github.com/vega/vl-convert) binary on `PATH`. Without it a
plot still draws in HTML output and in JupyterLab, and a PDF has no figure to
place.

## What it covers

- A Jupyter kernel for PHP 8.3 and later, on macOS and Linux.
- State across cells, so a variable bound in one cell is in scope in the next.
- Tracebacks that name the cell and the line a frame came from, rather than
  `eval()'d code`.
- Rich display for phibble tables and phiz plots, with `toMimeBundle()` and
  `toHtml()` hooks for any other class.
- Completion, `is_complete` for a front end's continuation prompt, and
  interruption through the stop button.
- Quarto's `.qmd` and JupyterLab, with cell options, figure captions, and HTML,
  `ipynb`, and PDF output.

## The phpstats family

juphyter is the notebook of the phpstats family.
[phibble](https://github.com/phpstats/phibble) provides data frames,
[phplyr](https://github.com/phpstats/phplyr) the dplyr verbs over them,
[phiz](https://github.com/phpstats/phiz) the plots, and
[phit](https://github.com/phpstats/phit) and
[CmdStanPHP](https://github.com/phpstats/CmdStanPHP) the models. juphyter
requires none of them and formats any of them that is installed.

[Get started](get-started.qmd) walks through a first notebook.
[Quarto](quarto.qmd) covers rendering a document, and
[JupyterLab](jupyter.qmd) covers the notebook interface.
